KAYAK appoints Peer Bueller as CEO, following Steve Hafner's transition to Executive Chair, to lead the travel search engine into a new era of innovation and growth.
Home » TRAVEL NEWS » KAYAK Announces Peer Bueller as CEO, Steve Hafner Shifts to Focus on AI Innovations in Travel · Published on February 3, 2026 · Image generated with Ai · KAYAK has named Peer Bueller as its new Chief Executive Officer, who will start his work immediately.
KAYAK has named Peer Bueller as its new Chief Executive Officer, who will start his work immediately. The move comes after Steve Hafner, the co-founder and long-time CEO of KAYAK, transitions into the role of Executive Chair.
The company now enters a new phase of development, which will drive its expansion into online travel innovation. Peer Bueller, who has been with KAYAK since 2016, brings a wealth of experience to the CEO role. Initially joining the company as Chief Financial Officer, Bueller added Chief Operating Officer to his responsibilities in 2021, playing a crucial role in KAYAK’s business expansion and growth.
As CEO, Bueller will continue to focus on strengthening KAYAK’s position as a leading travel search engine, while enhancing user experiences and driving the brand’s future growth strategies. With his deep expertise in finance and operations, Bueller is expected to steer the company toward new opportunities and innovations, especially in the growing digital travel space.

PR Newswire · February 3, 2026 2 min read · BKNG · +2.49% Co-Founder and Current CEO, Steve Hafner, named Executive Chair · NORWALK, Conn., Feb. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Booking Holdings, the world's leading provider of online travel and related services, and parent company of consumer-facing brands including Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, KAYAK and OpenTable, announced that Peer Bueller has been named Chief Executive Officer of KAYAK.
After 22 years as Co-Founder and CEO of KAYAK, Steve Hafner will become Executive Chair of KAYAK, and will take on a new leadership role at Booking Holdings focused on advancing AI innovation to support the company's long term ambitions.
"As CEO of KAYAK, I will continue to focus on making KAYAK everyone's favorite travel app, while raising the bar on our user experience and turning our strategy into results. We see a lot of opportunity ahead, and we're well positioned to pursue it," said new KAYAK CEO Peer Bueller.
"Steve pioneered the metasearch category with the launch of KAYAK and delivered industry-leading results for KAYAK for many years, since our acquisition of the brand in 2013," said Glenn Fogel, Chief Executive Officer of Booking Holdings. "We'll continue to rely on his entrepreneurialism, leadership and deep expertise in travel tech in his new role within Booking Holdings."

Kayak CEO and co-founder Steve Hafner is stepping down and handing the reins to CFO and COO Peer Bueller, parent company Booking Holdings announced Tuesday.  
After more than two decades leading the metasearch engine, Hafner will become executive chair of Kayak and also take on "a new leadership role at Booking Holdings," focusing on artificial intelligence innovation.  
"Steve pioneered the metasearch category with the launch of Kayak and delivered industry-leading results for Kayak for many years, since our acquisition of the brand in 2013," said Booking Holdings CEO Glenn Fogel.
Hafner said it’s the right time to hand responsibility over to Bueller, calling him "indispensable" to Kayak’s success.  
Bueller joined Kayak in 2016 as the company’s CFO, taking on additional responsibilities as COO in 2021. According to Booking Holdings, his focus has been on expansion, growing Kayak for Business and pushing commercial innovation.  
"As CEO of Kayak, I will continue to focus on making Kayak everyone's favorite travel app, while raising the bar on our user experience and turning our strategy into results. We see a lot of opportunity ahead, and we're well positioned to pursue it," Bueller said.  
Kayak was founded in 2004 by Hafner and co-founder Paul English, who stepped down in 2013.

results.name: Kayak CEO Steve Hafner Exits Post After 22 Years
results.content:
Parent company Booking Holdings announced Tuesday morning that it appointed chief financial officer Peer Bueller as Kayak CEO, and Hafner has become executive chair, a newly created position.
February 3, 2026 3 min read · BKNG · +0.71% Photo Credit: Skift · Kayak co-founder and CEO Steve Hafner, who took the company public in 2012 and sold it to Booking Holdings for $2.1 billion the next year, is out as CEO after 22 years. Parent company Booking Holdings announced Tuesday morning that it appointed chief financial officer Peer Bueller as Kayak CEO, and Hafner has become executive chair, a newly created position.
The company provided no further details on the new role. Bueller became Kayak CFO in 2016 and added chief operating officer to his duties in 2021. From 2012 to 2016, Bueller served as director of financial planning and analysis at the parent company's flagship brand, Booking.com. In addition to his Kayak CEO role, Hafner served as the CEO of sister brand OpenTable from January 2018 to August 2020.
Skift broke the news last month that Hafner had previously sought to take Kayak private, and had investors lined up to execute the move. Booking Holdings CEO Glenn Fogel rejected the idea, according to our scoop.
"Steve pioneered the metasearch category with the launch of Kayak and delivered industry-leading results for Kayak for many years, since our acquisition of the brand in 2013," said Glenn Fogel, Booking Holdings CEO, in a statement. "We'll continue to rely on his entrepreneurialism, leadership and deep expertise in travel tech in his new role within Booking Holdings."

For Booking Holdings, this leadership change at KAYAK lines up with a broader push to weave AI more tightly into how its brands surface travel options and handle complex search. Moving a long-tenured founder into an AI-focused role at the parent level, while elevating an operator with finance and expansion experience to CEO, suggests an effort to keep KAYAK execution-focused on products like KAYAK for Business and Events, while concentrating AI strategy across the wider group that includes Booking.com and Agoda.
Hafner's new AI-focused remit and Bueller's background in commercial and product growth at KAYAK for Business both point toward the same goal, using AI to improve trip planning and cross-sell across verticals in a way that can keep Booking competitive against other large travel players such as Expedia Group and Airbnb. ... 🎁 Leadership continuity at KAYAK, with a CEO who has been CFO and COO since 2016, may support operational stability while Booking integrates more AI across the group.
